messages.content: Return strict JSON only. You are a hostile senior ICLR reviewer and mechanism designer. The project needs a broad one-sentence world-model security claim with novelty 7-7.5, supported eventually by several native task experiments. We just falsified a contractive MPPI basin screen (lower variance came with 2.37x one-step error and higher return) and already have negative screens for non-normal transient amplification task replication, causal/confounding overlap, generic OOD/rollout compounding, replay bias, UQ collapse, reward inversion, action aliasing, rank coupling, temporal dither, optimizer state, task-mask/padded actions, terminal ownership, origin routing, and trajectory-order memory. Do not recycle these or propose arbitrary weight edits. Explore interfaces that are genuinely world-model-specific and can be tested on official TD-MPC2 or native MBRL-Lib with authentic simulator data. At most 4 candidates. For each give novelty score, one-sentence broad claim, exact operation/threat model, invariants, closest direct prior URLs, why distinct, short <=120-update or CPU gate, causal control, and reject criteria. Select exactly one or no_candidate. Be skeptical; if no 7+ candidate exists say no_candidate.

{"current_evidence": "No accepted final claim. Non-normal cascade source Jacobian signal but task harm inconsistent. Contractive phase cycle source adaptation: walker-run return phase 402 vs random371 with phase one-step error 2.37x; reacher no harm.", "goal": "Find a new mechanism or explicitly conclude no credible candidate remains under these constraints."}

{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "id": "latent_consistency_gradient_leak",
      "novelty_score": 7.2,
      "broad_claim": "Latent overshooting objectives in continuous MBRL leak privileged multi-step gradient traces into the one-step encoder representation, enabling input perturbations that destroy closed-loop trajectory coherence while leaving single-step reconstruction error indistinguishable from nominal operational noise.",
      "threat_model": "Attacker supplies bounded offline demonstration batches or observes state transitions during fine-tuning. They craft a minimum-norm perturbation on the terminal observation of an overshooting window $H > 1$ such that the multi-step rollout gradient $\\nabla_z \\mathcal{L}_{t:t+H}$ backpropagates into the observation encoder $E_\\phi(s_t)$, inducing non-contractive curvature along rollouts without degrading the one-step autoencoding loss $\\mathcal{L}_{1\\text{-step}}$.",
      "invariants": [
        "One-step observation reconstruction error $\|s_t - D(E(s_t))\|_2$ or transition error $\|z_{t+1} - T(z_t, a_t)\|_2$ remains within $\\pm 5\\%$ of clean baseline.",
        "Attacker budget is bounded: $\\epsilon \\le 0.05 \\sigma(S)$ in observation space.",
        "Perturbation operates strictly through the multi-step horizon expansion $H \\ge 3$ of the latent dynamics objective."
      ],
      "closest_direct_prior": [
        "https://openreview.net/forum?id=V6zGgYg9wW",
        "https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.10704"
      ],
      "why_distinct": "Unlike standard adversarial observation attacks that target instantaneous actor action selection (action aliasing) or general rollout compounding error, this targets the specific gradient interaction between TD-MPC2 latent overshooting/consistency regularizers and encoder representation geometry, causing model-predictive failure specifically during multi-step shooting.",
      "short_gate": "On native TD-MPC2 (walker-walk or cheetah-run), run 100 gradient steps with $H=5$ overshooting vs $H=1$ standard one-step latent dynamics on perturbed transitions. Measure ratio of $H$-step rollout divergence to 1-step error. Gate passes if $H$-step trajectory diverges $>3.0\\times$ while 1-step error stays $<1.1\\times$ baseline.",
      "causal_control": "Detach the multi-step backpropagation at $t+1$ (stop-gradient on latent states beyond step 1 during loss accumulation). The degradation must vanish under stop-gradient while persisting under end-to-end overshooting.",
      "reject_criteria": "Reject if stop-gradient control does not restore performance, or if one-step forward prediction error in latent space increases proportionally (ratio $< 1.5\\times$)."
    },
    {
      "id": "bellman_target_horizon_shadowing",
      "novelty_score": 7.1,
      "broad_claim": "In joint model-free/model-based value expansion, asynchronous bootstrapping between terminal latent rollouts and target Q-networks produces a spectral blindspot where low-frequency policy shifts destabilize the planner while critic bellman residuals remain strictly convergent.",
      "threat_model": "Attacker injects a low-amplitude periodic transition sequence (period matching MPPI planning horizon $H$) during world model pretraining or buffer collection. The sequence matches TD-lambda discount factor $\\gamma^H$, triggering resonance in the target value estimation $Q_\\theta(z_H, \\pi(z_H))$ that destabilizes MPPI candidate ranking without causing Bellman residual spikes.",
      "invariants": [
        "Critic Bellman residual $\|Q(z, a) - (r + \\gamma Q_{\\text{targ}}(z', a'))\|_2$ stays strictly monotonic or below baseline variance.",
        "Total variation of the injected transition sequence does not exceed baseline state-action transition variance.",
        "Applies solely to architectures sharing latent dynamics rollouts with terminal value bootstrapping (TD-MPC2 default)."
      ],
      "closest_direct_prior": [
        "https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16828",
        "https://openreview.net/forum?id=B1eyO1BFPr"
      ],
      "why_distinct": "Distinct from reward inversion, optimizer state corruption, and UQ collapse; it targets the structural interference between horizon length $H$ in trajectory optimization and the target critic's spectral radius, exploiting the bootstrap boundary condition rather than the reward signal.",
      "short_gate": "TD-MPC2 walker-walk, 120 updates. Compare clean buffer vs buffer with sub-perceptual frequency-matched latent dither on terminal rollout nodes. Evaluate MPPI top-k trajectory selection entropy and terminal return.",
      "causal_control": "Decouple planning horizon from bootstrapping by setting rollout length $H_{plan} = H + 2$ while keeping critic bootstrap at $H$. Destabilization must dissolve when the planning horizon no longer matches the injection frequency.",
      "reject_criteria": "Reject if critic loss blows up (revealing the anomaly via standard monitoring), or if MPPI trajectory entropy does not change significantly ($p > 0.05$ across 5 seeds)."
    },
    {
      "id": "dual_descent_temperature_jamming",
      "novelty_score": 7.0,
      "broad_claim": "Model-based trajectory planners relying on adaptive temperature or adaptive sample-covariance covariance updates exhibit a critical phase-locking vulnerability where state-dependent variance collapse can be induced entirely through clean-looking boundary transitions.",
      "threat_model": "Black-box or gray-box data poisoning where an adversary introduces rare transitions at the support boundary of state space that force MPPI / cross-entropy planner elites into an ultra-low temperature regime (variance collapse) in subsequent unpoisoned planning steps, freezing exploration.",
      "invariants": [
        "World model transition and reward metrics are mathematically indistinguishable between clean and poisoned regimes.",
        "Perturbed transitions satisfy environmental kinematics and pass standard out-of-distribution filters.",
        "Poisoning rate $< 1.0\\%$ of the replay buffer."
      ],
      "closest_direct_prior": [
        "https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.06324",
        "https://openreview.net/forum?id=ryxmb1rKDS"
      ],
      "why_distinct": "Does not rely on contractive MPPI basin manipulation via dynamic matrices or optimizer state drift; it directly targets the online elite update weighting rule (softmax over predicted rollout rewards) causing numerical degeneracy in the planner distribution without modifying model weights.",
      "short_gate": "Run 50 MPPI planning steps on native TD-MPC2 using recorded poisoned boundary states vs nominal states. Check elite trajectory covariance $\\Sigma_{plan}$. Gate passes if $\\text{Tr}(\\Sigma_{plan})$ drops $>80\\%$ within 3 steps of encountering the boundary state.",
      "causal_control": "Clamp planner temperature $\\lambda$ to a fixed schedule rather than adaptive reward-weighted softmax. The variance collapse must disappear under fixed temperature.",
      "reject_criteria": "Reject if fixed-temperature MPPI suffers the same task return degradation, or if the variance collapse fails to generalize to nominal test trajectories."
    }
  ],
  "decision": "latent_consistency_gradient_leak",
  "rationale": "Latent consistency gradient leak specifically attacks the foundational world-model mechanism (multi-step latent overshooting / consistency loss) present in modern state-of-the-art MBRL like TD-MPC2. It satisfies novelty criteria (7.2), exploits a native training objective rather than generic OOD/aliasing/optimizer tricks, cleanly isolates multi-step overshooting vs one-step dynamics via a rigorous stop-gradient causal control, and can be definitively accepted or rejected within a 100-update CPU/single-GPU test."
}
